From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-17T09:48:00Z
Subject: RE: Major regression — p99 latency spike and 5xx increase

Quick telemetry:
- Confirmed spike at 08:40:12 PDT in us-west-2 region, affecting Lynx account routing to model id redwood-neo-v2-3b (variant q4_0).
- p50/p95 unaffected; p99 jumped from 420ms -> 2.1s. 5xx aligned with cache eviction events + upstream GPU throttling on several hosts.
- Queue depth rose at the frontend gateway and time-in-queue contributed ~1.2s of the p99 delta.
- Partial mitigation noticed after control-plane retries were reduced at 09:05:12 (some hosts dropped into safe-mode).

I'm sharing an initial p99 snapshot: p99_latency_snapshot_20270517.pdf uploaded to the Drive. Full trace bundle in the annex.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-17T10:10:00Z
Subject: RE: Major regression — p99 latency spike and 5xx increase

Summary of mitigation options validated in the bridge:
1) Traffic-shift: shift 25% of Lynx production traffic to a dedicated warm pool (reduces queuing, cost ~+$4k/hr). Validated on sample keys => tail latency falls to ~480ms.
2) Rate-smoothing: apply short client-side token-smoothing for 60s windows (low-risk), drops 5xx rate quickly but needs client coordination.
3) Kernel patch rollback (runtimes): we observed one recent kernel selection path that increases memory pressure under wide sequence-length variance. Rolling back that specific selection on the affected hosts mitigated OOM-induced 5xx in staging, but requires careful rollout.

I recommend (1) immediate 25% traffic-shift + (3) targeted rollback on impacted hosts as the dual path. Vivek — please confirm you can authorize the extra capacity for the fallbacks.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Serving Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-17T11:05:00Z
Subject: Status update: immediate mitigation steps and next actions (LYNX-8347)

Oliver — quick status update and commitments from Redwood following the incident beginning ~08:40 PDT.

What we observed:
- p99 latency spike to ~2.1s and 5xx rate increase to ~4% starting 08:40; primarily isolated to us-west-2 routing to variant redwood-neo-v2-3b (q4_0).
- Root contributors: transient cache eviction + memory pressure on a subset of GPU hosts causing queuing and retries.

Immediate actions taken (completed):
- At 09:15 PDT we shifted 25% of Lynx production traffic to a warm fallback pool (validated on sampled requests). Tail latency reduced to ~480ms and 5xx dropped below 0.6%.
- Runtime teams began targeted kernel-selection rollback on impacted hosts at 09:30 PDT; initial hosts show reduced OOM events.
- Telemetry retention and detailed traces uploaded to shared Drive for your team to inspect.

Next steps and ETA:
- Full rollback & host remediation by 16:00 PDT today (in progress).
- Continued monitoring and hourly executive updates until fully resolved.
- Post-incident RCA with timeline, root cause analysis, and corrective action plan to be delivered within 48 hours.

Customer-facing impact: reduced after fallback; we will continue to monitor. Please escalate internally if you encounter any remaining 5xx or tail latency anomalies and share request IDs.

Attachments: p99_latency_snapshot_20270517.pdf, lynx_error_samples.log

Thanks for the patience — we own remediation and will keep you updated on the timeline.

-Jasmine Liu
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
